Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across business and general-news outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's resignation amid a spy-affair scandal, which is reshaping conversations about AI industry leadership, China export policy, and market stability. The imminent Anthropic IPO and a worldwide Microsoft outage are the other major threads tying together outlets this week.

stories.headline: Nvidia Board Urged to Weigh Reinstating Jensen Huang as Scandal Fallout Widens
stories.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned amid affair allegations including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, and two major shareholders, Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides' Gavin Baker, are now pressing the board to leave open the possibility of his return rather than rushing a permanent successor. The saga has triggered congressional testimony demands, shareholder lawsuits, and a roughly $450 billion hit to Nvidia's market value.

stories.headline: Congress Moves to Pass Tighter AI Chip Export Rules Following Nvidia Scandal
stories.summary: FT reports that Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy has added momentum for lawmakers to tighten U.S. export restrictions on AI chips reaching China. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is also facing scrutiny over his handling of the Megaspeed export-control investigation tied to the affair.

stories.headline: Anthropic Prices Record IPO Targeting Over $1 Trillion Valuation Amid AI Market Jitters
stories.summary: Anthropic set terms for what could be one of the largest IPOs ever, with the company seeking to raise up to $62.5 billion at a market cap that could top $1 trillion. The offering, expected to begin trading this week, is being closely watched as a referendum on the broader AI trade just as Nvidia's leadership crisis has rattled investor confidence.

stories.headline: Microsoft Says All Services Restored After Day-Long Global Outage
stories.summary: Microsoft said it completed efforts to fix a global outage that had disrupted Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, affecting communications at hospitals, police departments, and government services worldwide.

stories.headline: Data Centre Construction Stocks Lose $4.2tn as AI Trade Boom Unravels
stories.summary: Shares in AI infrastructure 'picks and shovels' companies have been hit hard by a broader tech selloff, with data center construction stocks collectively losing trillions in value as skepticism grows about the pace of the AI buildout.

stories.headline: SpaceX Makes History With Successful Rocket Catch in Texas
stories.summary: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned from orbit and landed at the same site where it launched, marking a milestone toward the company's goal of fully reusable rockets.

stories.headline: Family Dollar to Pay $63 Million Settlement for Overcharging Customers
stories.summary: The discount retailer agreed to a $63 million settlement after federal regulators and 17 states alleged it had been overcharging shoppers at checkout since 2023.

stories.headline: Crypto's Slow-Motion Selloff Leaves Traders Weary and Hopeless
stories.summary: Bitcoin's latest decline is testing even committed crypto investors as prices approach their lowest levels of the year amid broader market turbulence.

Business.gaps: No recent business-relevant items were found for Business Insider or Puck. Politico's recent output in the feed was limited to general political stories (Alaska governor race, NY politics) without a clear business angle.

US politics.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by the fallout from Democrats' sweeping Nov. 3 midterm victories, especially the fight over who leads Senate Democrats and how Republicans regrouped under Thune. Secondary threads include the Supreme Court's new asylum case, the lame-duck legislative agenda, and continuing fallout from the Nvidia/Jensen Huang spy scandal.

stories.headline: Van Hollen's insurgent challenge to Schumer roils Senate Democrats
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is mounting the first contested Senate Democratic leadership race in over 30 years, challenging Chuck Schumer ahead of a Dec. 1 secret-ballot vote, with Schumer currently holding more public endorsements (14 to 5) but needing 28-29 votes to win.

stories.headline: Thune survives bruising post-election leadership fight
stories.summary: Senate Republicans kept John Thune as leader by acclamation after a contentious closed-door meeting in which conservative critics demanded a lame-duck strategy roadmap before voting, with one lawmaker comparing the session to "Festivus."

stories.headline: Democrats chart post-midterm path at Denver conference as blue wave reshapes states
stories.summary: Democrats from across the country gathered in Denver for a two-day conference to plot strategy after midterm wins that also ended long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures and will give women a record number of state legislative seats.

stories.headline: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins flips Alaska's governorship
stories.summary: Politico reports it is the first time Alaskans have elected a Democrat to the corner office in over two decades, part of the broader post-midterm realignment in the state.

stories.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear case on Trump's asylum suspension
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will take up a challenge to the Trump administration's "invasion"-based asylum ban at the southern border, a case Roll Call notes will put a signature immigration policy before the justices.

stories.headline: GOP's lame-duck agenda centers on judicial confirmations and defense funding
stories.summary: Sen. Kevin Cramer said Senate Republicans will prioritize confirming Trump's federal judge nominees and advancing a reconciliation package to fund defense during their final weeks controlling the chamber, with Thune touting 58 confirmed judges so far this Congress.

stories.headline: Trump's economic advisers clash over Commerce's handling of Nvidia spy scandal
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports Treasury Secretary pointed blame at Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over the department's investigation into whether Megaspeed, tied to the Jensen Huang spy-sex scandal, breached export restrictions; The Guardian similarly reports Lutnick faces questions over what senior officials knew.

stories.headline: Pentagon prepares its own prosecution of general accused of leaking
stories.summary: Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia now faces legal jeopardy on two fronts after allegations from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's team were previously referred to the Justice Department, according to the Washington Post.

US politics.gaps: Could not verify current leading stories from NYT or WSJ beyond the single feed items provided, as these outlets block web search; National Review and Washington Examiner's recent output leaned toward opinion/culture pieces rather than hard news, limiting usable items from those outlets this cycle.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation over an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and by Anthropic's blockbuster, oversubscribed IPO this week. Secondary threads include a nationwide FAA ground stop blamed on legacy equipment, Tesla's limited Cybercab rollout, and new evidence of Chinese AI labs circumventing chip export controls.

stories.headline: Nvidia's leadership crisis deepens after Jensen Huang's ouster
stories.summary: Nvidia's security chief quietly departed in August, raising fresh questions about oversight just as Jensen Huang stepped down over his relationship with an executive at a firm suspected of helping funnel chips to China; a petition backed by Elon Musk and other tech executives calling for Huang's reinstatement had passed 115,000 signatures. The Information reported that the resignation left 'far more questions than answers,' while Rest of World and Techmeme note Asian governments and insiders are scrambling to assess the fallout.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO is six times oversubscribed, on track to be the largest ever
stories.summary: Anthropic is on track for the largest IPO ever, with orders exceeding available shares by a factor of six, as the company targets a roughly $1.4 trillion valuation and Nvidia itself buys $10 billion of stock through a concurrent private placement. CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon he hopes the offering will 'underpromise and overdeliver,' even as he separately admitted deep uncertainty about compute spending heading into next year.

stories.headline: FAA's nationwide ground stop traced to copper-wire replacement work
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday's nationwide ground stop, the FAA's third ever, stemmed from routine work replacing outdated copper wiring with fiber, and FAA administrator Bryan Bedford stressed there was 'zero evidence of anything AI-related.' Ars Technica and The Register also covered the outage and its causes, while Ars separately reported the FAA has been expanding AI-based tools to manage air traffic congestion without involving the controllers' union.

stories.headline: Tesla opens limited Cybercab pre-orders with steep monthly fee
stories.summary: Tesla began inviting select customers to pre-order a Cybercab 'for personal use,' complete with geographic restrictions and a $299 monthly subscription fee that even Elon Musk conceded is too high. The Verge noted the fine print tempers Tesla's autonomous-future marketing, as the offer applies only to a limited pool of buyers for now.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs reportedly training on Nvidia's Blackwell chips despite export controls
stories.summary: A forensic report cited by an ex-OpenAI engineer claims to have found Blackwell's technical fingerprint in models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group, suggesting Chinese labs are accessing restricted Nvidia hardware despite U.S. export controls. The finding lands amid heightened scrutiny of chip-smuggling routes following the Jensen Huang scandal.

stories.headline: South Korea's top exam scorer admits using AI to cheat
stories.summary: A test-taker who scored near-perfectly on a South Korean national exam admitted to sending photos of questions to an AI tool, stoking fears of similar cheating ahead of next week's national college entrance exam.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for agent-driven purchases
stories.summary: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Wallet, a company-stated 'secure way for agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots to complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections,' extending its agentic commerce push.

stories.headline: Meituan releases giant agent model trained entirely without Nvidia chips
stories.summary: Meituan released weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model built and trained entirely on Chinese hardware, scoring 88.4 on Terminal Bench and landing just behind leading Western models—underscoring China's push toward Nvidia-independent AI infrastructure.

Tech & AI.gaps: IEEE Spectrum and 404 Media had no recent items directly on this group's main storylines (Nvidia/Anthropic); their available pieces were tangential (microcredentials for AI governance, monkeys watching Minions). Google DeepMind had no company announcements found in the last 48 hours on this topic.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the aftermath of COP31 in Antalya, with outlets focused on a steep drop in climate-finance pledges and UN Secretary-General Guterres's parting attack on fossil fuel interests. Energy-focused outlets are also tracking fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and its ripple effects on AI data-center power deals, nuclear project delays in Canada and the US, Exxon's legal challenge to EU carbon capture rules, and rising US energy prices feeding inflation and Fed rate-hike expectations.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Nvidia resignation throws AI data-center energy boom into fresh chaos
stories.summary: Heatmap reports Huang's departure is rattling the AI buildout just as the same dispatch notes China signed a $15 billion deal to sell 7 gigawatts of solar, wind, storage and transmission infrastructure to Turkey at COP31, and California ordered its big utilities to build a common framework for virtual power plants.

stories.headline: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis finds the amount of public funding pledged to help developing countries tackle climate change has dropped by more than 70% in 2026, as most prior multi-year pledges expired and the US withdrew from international climate efforts while European aid budgets were cut.

stories.headline: UN chief's closing COP31 message: fossil fuels are 'killing our planet'
stories.summary: In what Heatmap describes as likely his final speech before the summit as UN chief, Guterres railed against a world still on what he called the path to mutually assured destruction, accusing fossil fuel interests of profiting while the planet suffers.

stories.headline: Exxon sues the EU over carbon capture rules
stories.summary: Exxon Mobil filed a confidential legal challenge to the European Union's carbon capture regulations, which the Financial Times called the latest attempt by the US energy giant to roll back Brussels' flagship green rules.

stories.headline: Leading small modular nuclear reactor project in Canada will be late and over budget
stories.summary: Ontario Power Generation said its first BWRX-300 unit at the Darlington site will miss its October 2030 target and blow past its $7.7 billion Canadian budget, underscoring persistent timeline and cost challenges for North American nuclear builds.

stories.headline: US energy prices keep climbing, pushing inflation and rate-hike expectations higher
stories.summary: Heatmap reports October's 0.4% overall price rise was led partly by energy costs climbing 0.7%, with gasoline up 37% year-over-year and Maine heating oil prices up 80%, a jump that analysts say makes a December Fed rate hike more likely.

stories.headline: California's climate disclosure laws partly survive appeals court ruling
stories.summary: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals allowed California's scope 1 and scope 2 emissions reporting under SB 253 to proceed while halting enforcement of scope 3 reporting and a related climate-risk disclosure law, SB 261.

Energy.gaps: Latitude Media and Argus Media had no recent energy coverage found via search; E&E News search results returned only older archived stories outside the 48-hour window. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT and The Economist block search, and their feed items provided (Anthropic's IPO, Nvidia chip smuggling) were tech-focused rather than energy/climate stories, so they are not reflected here.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Taiwanese and Western outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid a China-espionage scandal, and by the run-up to the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral at next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen. Business and economy outlets are also tracking China's surging AI-driven export data, a battery-swap station race between CATL and Nio, and continued scrutiny of US-China tech and talent flows.

stories.headline: China sees Nvidia chief Huang's swift downfall as political hit
stories.summary: Chinese officials and commentators are framing Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as CEO over an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy as a political hit rather than a personal scandal, with some saying he was targeted for being ethnic Chinese. Nvidia's board has said it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised, while the episode is fueling a Washington push for tighter chip export curbs.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China
stories.summary: The White House confirmed Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first-ever three-way meeting between the three leaders on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19, with nuclear arms reduction and the Iran war expected to feature but not the Ukraine conflict. Chinese state media say Xi will chair the Shenzhen gathering and push a China-led AI cooperation agenda as a rival to Washington's chip-control initiatives.

stories.headline: China's Exports Jump on Strong AI Trade
stories.summary: China's exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier, beating forecasts as AI-related shipments of chips and computing equipment sustained rapid growth even as car exports slowed sharply. Imports also surged 41.6%, with much of the export gain driven by rising prices rather than larger shipment volumes.

stories.headline: CATL targets 6,000 passenger car battery swap stations in 2027, potentially overtaking Nio
stories.summary: Battery giant CATL plans 5,000 urban and 1,000 highway swap stations covering 297 Chinese cities by 2027, a build-out that could put it ahead of current market leader Nio in the fast-growing battery-swap segment.

stories.headline: The Massive Chinese Spy Operation Targeting Western Tech and AI
stories.summary: WSJ reporting examines a broad Chinese espionage effort aimed at Western technology and AI firms, a story that has gained new urgency amid the Jensen Huang scandal and related congressional scrutiny.

stories.headline: Spies and silicon chips: Alice Huang's tangled corporate web
stories.summary: An AFP investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed, the company tied to the woman at the center of the Jensen Huang affair, found the firm dealt in billions of dollars of advanced AI chips while its office appeared to be an empty shell. Caixin has separately reported that the woman, Alice Huang, has ties to a Shanghai fund manager who came under criminal scrutiny.

stories.headline: China Poached This Top Harvard Professor. Now He Wants Others to Join Him.
stories.summary: WSJ profiles Liu Jun's move from Beijing to Boston and back as emblematic of a broader exodus of Chinese scholars from US universities, as Beijing works to recruit top academic talent back home.

stories.headline: COMAC's CE-25A Electric Commercial Aircraft Completes Its First Crewed Flight
stories.summary: China's state-backed planemaker COMAC flew its 19-seat CE-25A electric aircraft with two pilots and a flight test engineer aboard for the first time, covering just over 60 kilometers in under 17 minutes.

China.gaps: No recent items could be found for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, CGTN, Yicai Global, TechNode or Xinhua; Reuters, AP and The Economist blocked search so only their feed items (none provided for this group) could be used.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the widening regional war: Iran's renewed drone and missile attacks on Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, a Houthi advance that hands them control of the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint, and a senior Hamas commander's killing in Gaza. Israeli outlets are absorbed in the post-election scramble between Netanyahu and Eisenkot over forming a unity government, while business titles (AGBI, Arabian Business) are tracking the war's toll on Saudi markets, UAE industry and new Gulf investment deals with China.

stories.headline: Iran escalates attacks on Bahrain and Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched a drone strike on a US-linked radar site in Bahrain and the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and three drones over the Eastern Province, part of an intensifying low-level conflict. Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Jordan all condemned the Iranian strikes on Bahrain, which called on the UN Security Council to act.

stories.headline: Yemeni government forces retreat, handing Houthis control of Bab el-Mandeb Strait
stories.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces withdrew from territory overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a retreat that analysts say hands Iran-aligned Houthi rebels greater leverage over one of the world's key maritime chokepoints for global shipping.

stories.headline: Senior Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
stories.summary: Hamas said a senior commander who had helped plan and oversee the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel was killed in an Israeli strike in southern Gaza, continuing Israel's pattern of targeting replacement commanders before they can rebuild Hamas's command structure.

stories.headline: Netanyahu and Eisenkot clash over Israeli unity government
stories.summary: Caretaker PM Benjamin Netanyahu renewed calls for a national unity government citing the Iran nuclear threat, while Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot, who holds the mandate to form a government, dismissed the offer as a "bluff" even as Likud and Yashar negotiating teams met to discuss a potential coalition.

stories.headline: Three oil tankers catch fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state media, underscoring the continued danger to shipping through the critical oil corridor.

stories.headline: Jordan sentences three men to death over Karak church attack
stories.summary: A Jordanian court sentenced three men to death by hanging over a deadly shooting attack on a church in Karak, and the kingdom cancelled Christmas celebrations in solidarity with victims' families.

stories.headline: Saudi stocks rebound but war damage still weighs on Gulf industry
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's All-Shares Index closed the week 9 percent above its October five-year low but remained down 2 percent year-to-date, with recovery led by state-backed firms like Aramco-adjacent Acwa and Saudi National Bank even as Houthi missile threats keep pressuring profit margins. Separately, UAE-based Emirates Global Aluminium reported its debt rose 40 percent to $5 billion after an Iranian attack damaged its Al Taweelah smelter, cutting revenue 16 percent.

stories.headline: Oman signs multibillion-dollar investment package with China
stories.summary: Oman's sovereign wealth fund announced its largest-ever single-day package of investment agreements with Chinese institutions, including an $800 million joint fund with China's Silk Road Fund, highlighting growing Gulf competition to attract Chinese capital.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find recent (last 24-48h) region-relevant coverage from Khaleej Times, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Ynetnews or Iran International within the search allowance; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, The Economist and BBC block search so only WSJ feed items were available among that group.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across African and international outlets this week centers on the DRC's Ebola outbreak disrupting mining operations and schools, US geopolitical maneuvering in Congo and West Africa's critical minerals sector, and a cluster of economic stories spanning mining deals, tech outages, and aviation fuel shortages. Politics coverage is dominated by election delays in South Sudan and security crackdowns in Burkina Faso, while business desks are watching De Beers, Mozambique's national carrier, and Big Tech's grip on African infrastructure.

stories.headline: Barrick furloughs employees at Congo's Kibali gold mine as Ebola precaution
stories.summary: Barrick Mining is furloughing staff and subcontractors at its Kibali gold mine in DR Congo after officials reported two Ebola deaths in a nearby community, according to an internal memo cited by Reuters.

stories.headline: Trump picks pastor and early backer as US ambassador to the DRC
stories.summary: John Mark Burns, a South Carolina preacher with no diplomatic experience, has been tapped to fill a DRC ambassadorial post left vacant for almost a year as Washington tightens its grip on Congo's cobalt sector.

stories.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers under Anglo's proposed exit
stories.summary: Angola is seeking a 10% holding in De Beers as part of Anglo American's proposed sale of its stake in the major diamond producer, a mines ministry spokesperson told Reuters.

stories.headline: AirMozambique warns of flight cancellations due to fuel shortage
stories.summary: Mozambique's national carrier warned that fuel supply restrictions in the country mean it may have to cancel some flights.

stories.headline: South Sudan postpones first general election from December to February
stories.summary: The elections commission says the delay will allow for additional processes including distribution of registration materials and civic education ahead of the country's first national vote.

stories.headline: US quietly counters China and Russia in West Africa's mining sector
stories.summary: Washington is hunting for gold and lithium in Mali, moving to muscle in against entrenched Chinese and Russian players amid opaque deals and intensifying geopolitical rivalry.

stories.headline: Microsoft's 18-hour outage exposed South Africa's dependence on Big Tech
stories.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted South African businesses and public institutions including Eskom, Absa and FlySafair, highlighting the country's growing reliance on Big Tech's cloud infrastructure.

stories.headline: Burkina Faso issues arrest warrants for around 20 people, including journalists
stories.summary: The warrants target exiled journalists, activists, a former minister and ex-military officers who face terrorism-related charges.

Africa.gaps: Africa Confidential, The Continent and African Business were checked via web search only (site search, no direct access), and nothing dated within the strict last-24-48h window beyond items already reflected could be confirmed as newly published; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and had no relevant feed items provided for this beat.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days is dominated by Saturday Night Live's topical cold open and monologue referencing the Jensen Huang/Nvidia scandal and the FAA ground stop, alongside a wave of stories on network cost-cutting (CNN, ABC, CBS), publisher battles with AI platforms, and post-midterm scrutiny of political journalism and press freedom.

stories.headline: SNL's John Mulaney-hosted episode skewers Jensen Huang scandal, RFK Jr. and FAA chaos
stories.summary: Bowen Yang made a surprise return to play ousted Nvidia chief Jensen Huang in a cold open mocking tech billionaires' vulnerability to honey-pot plots, while host John Mulaney used his monologue to mock HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

stories.headline: Status details wave of cost-cutting and contract anxiety across CNN, ABC and CBS
stories.summary: Oliver Darcy's Status has run consecutive dispatches this week on turmoil inside TV news divisions, including pieces titled 'CNN's Contract Cliff,' 'Facing the Exits,' 'ABC's Cost-Cutting Anxiety' and 'The CBS-CNN Cashout,' pointing to deepening financial pressure at major networks.

stories.headline: UK watchdog probes Meta's AI scraping terms as publishers warn of revenue hit
stories.summary: Press Gazette reports that trade group Digital Content Next told a court that AI content retrieval is "already eating away" at publisher businesses, as the UK's Competition and Markets Authority opened an investigation into whether Meta's proposed scraping terms could "unfairly harm" publishers.

stories.headline: The Atlantic keeps hiring despite questions over its business strategy
stories.summary: Dylan Byers writes that The Atlantic's announcement of another new round of writer hires continues what he calls a "curious business strategy" of expanding editorial headcount at a magazine-identified brand owned by Laurene Powell Jobs.

stories.headline: Cravath employee charged with insider trading tied to Paramount-Warner Bros. deal
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors charged a Cravath employee with insider trading, alleging the person netted $70,000 in profits using confidential information related to client matters including Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros.

stories.headline: Democrats weigh using new congressional control to shore up press freedom
stories.summary: Poynter reports that within 48 hours of Democrats securing both chambers of Congress, Senator Richard Blumenthal emailed the FCC demanding records as part of a press-freedom-related investigation.

stories.headline: Democratic-funded 'pink slime' local news sites surface in Ohio midterms
stories.summary: CJR examines how NorthStar Civic Media, which brands itself as independent local reporting, was founded by a former Democratic campaign staffer and received over a million dollars in Meta ad spending from Democratic funders promoting its sites.

stories.headline: Savannah Guthrie re-ups at Today as NBC News cancels streaming show Stay Tuned
stories.summary: Adweek reports Savannah Guthrie is staying on NBC's Today after a contract extension, noting that NBC News has canceled the primetime program Stay Tuned, which aired on NBC News Now.

Media.gaps: NYT, FT and The Guardian provided no media-industry feed items and block web search, so no current leads could be gathered for them.
